Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Church life

ceremony noun

also ceremonies, ceremonial, rite, ritual, solemn occasion, opening ceremony

classical

Liv. 38.57 (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 7.3: sollemne clāvī fīgendī (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. ceremony

sollemne, sollemnis n.

noun, third declension

a ceremony, a solemn rite or festival

The neuter of sollemnis “yearly, established, solemn”: any formal ceremony, sacred or civic, as Livy uses it. Lewis & Short notes it is perhaps not in Cicero, who says sollemnia sacra, lūdī sollemnēs.

Other words

  • caerimōnia, caerimōniae f. — a religious ceremony, a sacred rite

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.187: occultissimīs caerimōniīs (Lewis & Short)

    Only of worship, mostly in the plural; in the singular more often reverence or sanctity.

  • rītus, rītūs m. — a rite; the manner of a ceremony

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.7: sacra dīs aliīs Albānō rītū, Graecō Herculī facit (Lewis & Short)

    The form a rite follows, the way it is done (Graecō rītū), and so “custom” in general (rītū, in the manner of).

  • sollemnitās, sollemnitātis f. — a solemnity, a ceremony

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · M-O s.v. ceremony

    Late Latin, as in the Church’s solemnities.

Examples

  • inter pūblicum sollemne spōnsālibus rīte factīs

    the betrothal was duly made at a public ceremonyLiv. 38.57

See also wedding, religious.
